title: Service & Machine Token Naming, Rotation Automation, and Audit Migration
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Background:
Redwood currently has multiple overlapping conventions and ad-hoc scripts for API key and service token lifecycle. This ticket scopes a cross-team initiative to introduce a single, human- and machine- friendly naming convention, automated rotation lanes (short/medium/long lived), and a migration path for existing tokens into the audit-ready ledger used by RBAC v2 and audit logging pipelines. The work touches token creation flows, the admin console, backend rotation workers, and audit event schemas.

Goals:
1) Standardize naming so tokens are immediately identifiable (owner team, environment, purpose, and a short non-sensitive hash), enabling faster incident response and better auditability.
2) Implement rotation automation for short-lived machine tokens (default 24h), medium-lived tokens (7d), and an exceptions workflow for long-lived tokens (90d max, managerial approval).
3) Ensure all lifecycle events (create, rotate, revoke, expire) are consistently emitted to the audit stream with sufficient metadata to reconstruct token lineage and used scopes.
4) Provide a non-disruptive migration path for existing tokens with a grace and conversion window and a one-click migration tool for owners via Console.

Scope / Non-Goals:
- In scope: token naming conventions, rotation worker implementation, token ledger events, Console UX for rotation and exception requests, audit schema changes, and migration tooling.
- Out of scope: full RBAC policy language redesign (handled in RBAC v2 epic), underlying KMS storage changes except for metadata tagging, or replacing customer-managed KMS flows.

Design highlights (summary):
- Naming convention proposal: <team>-<env>-<purpose>-<shorthash>-v<semver> (example: payments-prod-ingest-4f3a6-v2). For machine tokens created by the platform the <team> can be the service name; for human tokens we prefix HUMAN-. Shorthash is 6 chars derived from HMAC of the key id (not secret).
- Token types and automation lanes: SHORT (24h auto-rotate), MEDIUM (7d auto-rotate), LONG (up to 90d, requires exception ticket tag and approval, owner must justify).
- Rotation approach: double-write issuance pattern: new token issued and written to ledger before marking old token tombstoned; clients receive rotation metadata endpoint that supports two-token acceptance windows to allow zero-downtime swap.
- Audit events: standardize on event types token.created, token.rotated, token.revoked, token.expired, token.retired plus fields: token_id, key_name, owner, team, environment, scopes, rotation_policy, previous_token_id, action_initiator (API / user id), request_id, and timestamp. Events are emitted to the existing audit pipeline topic with a low-latency path to Console retention and long-term S3.

Migration plan (high level):
Phase 1 (Read-only discovery): run a discovery job that enumerates existing tokens, owners, last_seen and policy. A Confluence report + Console view will allow owners to opt-in to automated naming/rotation.
Phase 2 (Opt-in conversion): provide a one-click conversion in Console that issues a new token under the new naming/rotation lane and deprecates the old token with a 7-day overlap window.
Phase 3 (Bulk sweep): for tokens that do not opt-in after 60 days, execute a bulk rotation job that creates a replacement short-lived token and emails the owner. Emergency exceptions allowed via documented process.

Acceptance criteria:
- New tokens created via API/Console conform to naming pattern and include policy tags (rotation_policy, team, env, purpose).
- Rotation worker successfully rotates a short token with no client-visible downtime in our staging environment for 95% of test cases.
- Audit pipeline receives and indexes token lifecycle events containing the required fields for lineage reconstruction.
- Console shows token lineage and tombstone state for migrated and rotated tokens.
- Migration tool demonstrated in a canary with two product teams and validated by security review.

Risks & mitigations:
- Client compatibility: some internal services don't support token swapping; mitigation: two-token acceptance window + temporary ‘compat-mode’ flag per service with telemetry.
- Owner notification fatigue during bulk rotation: mitigation: staggered batches, email + Slack+ Console banners, runbook for rollback.
- Audit schema bloat: mitigation: incremental schema additions and retention policy; cost analysis in release notes.

Metrics to measure success:
- Percentage of active tokens following new naming pattern (target 90% by +90 days).
- Mean time to rotate (MTTR) for short tokens.
- Number of manual long-lived exception approvals.
- Audit event ingestion lag (target <30s for token lifecycle events).

acceptance_criteria: Tokens created after rollout have platform-enforced naming tags and rotation_policy metadata.
Rotation worker rotates SHORT lane tokens in staging with <1% failure for canonical clients.
Audit stream contains canonical lifecycle events for rotated tokens and indexes owner/team/env fields.
Migration tool completes opt-in conversion with lineage visible in Console and no auth interruptions for canary teams.
Security sign-off on exception workflow and long-lived token process.
rollback_plan: If rotation worker causes auth failures above threshold, flip worker to read-only mode (stop issuing replacements), enable manual rollback: re-enable previous tokens from tombstone via ledger restore endpoint, alert owners, and revert Console migration UI to previous state. Run immediate hotfix to add larger acceptance window or compatibility flag as needed.
migration_plan: Discovery -> opt-in conversion -> 60-day warn -> staggered bulk sweep. Provide per-token owner contact, automatic ticket creation when conversion fails, and a failed-migration dashboard. Require sign-off for any token included in bulk sweep marked 'critical'.
implementation_notes: Use existing audit topic (audit.events) with new event schema version v2-token-life; ensure backwards-compatible consumers
Rotation worker will run in Dedicated infra pool with retry/backoff and jitter; use idempotent issuance APIs
Shorthash generation must be irreversible; store only token_id mappings in DB, not secrets
Integrate SSO/SAML user tokens by tying HUMAN- prefixed keys to SAML assertion id and requiring re-auth during exception requests
